# Use a common base image like Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installers to avoid prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI libraries, git, required certificates, libgomp1, and python3
# Corrected: Added python3 as a build dependency for the LAMMPS cmake process
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    gfortran \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    ca-certificates \
    libgomp1 \
    python3 && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI environment variables for container compatibility
# This allows MPI to run as root and oversubscribe resources, which is common in Kubernetes
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Clone the latest branch of the LAMMPS source code from the official repository
# Using --depth 1 significantly reduces the clone size
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /opt/lammps-src

# Build LAMMPS from source using CMake
# Enable the REAXFF package as required by the 'lammps-reax' application
# This is a CPU-only build with MPI enabled
RUN cd /opt/lammps-src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
        -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
        ../cmake && \
    make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled LAMMPS executable to a system-wide location on the PATH
# This makes the 'lmp' command available globally
RUN cp /opt/lammps-src/build/lmp /usr/local/bin/

# Set up the working directory for application runs
WORKDIR /app

# Copy all files from the ReaxFF HNS example directory into the WORKDIR
# These can be used as a starting point or for validation
RUN cp /opt/lammps-src/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/

# Clean up the system to reduce the final image size
# Remove build-only dependencies and the downloaded source code
# Corrected: Added python3 to the purge list
RUN apt-get purge -y --auto-remove \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    gfortran \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    python3 && \
    rm -rf /opt/lammps-src

# Set the default command to run the LAMMPS executable
# This will print the help message if no arguments are provided
CMD ["lmp"]

# This manifest defines a Flux MiniCluster to run a LAMMPS simulation.
# It is configured for a single-node execution on an AWS CPU instance within Kubernetes.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster resource.
  name: lammps-reax-test
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 1 for single-node execution.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run.
  # The lmp command uses a 2x2x2 process grid, so we request 8 tasks.
  tasks: 8

  # If set to true, the Operator will not delete the pods when the job is complete.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging modes for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Fail on any error, do not continue.
    strict: true

  # Defines the container that will run the HPC application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command is run by `flux run`. Do not add `flux run` here.
      # The input file 'in.reaxff.hns' is expected to be in the container's working directory.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This container runs the main job, not a script to launch it.
      launcher: false

# This manifest provides a corrected MiniCluster configuration for a LAMMPS simulation.
# The fix addresses the "unsatisfiable request" error by aligning the number of tasks
# with the available resources recognized by Flux.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster resource.
  name: lammps-reax-test
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster job remains 1 for single-node execution.
  size: 1

  # Corrected: The number of tasks is set to 1.
  # Without explicit CPU resource requests, Flux assumes only one allocatable CPU slot
  # is available in the pod. The previous value of 8 caused an allocation failure
  # because the job requested more tasks (8) than available slots (1).
  # This change ensures the job request is satisfiable.
  tasks: 1

  # If set to true, the Operator will not delete the pods when the job is complete.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging modes for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Fail on any error, do not continue.
    strict: true

  # Defines the container that will run the HPC application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command is unchanged. LAMMPS will adapt and run this on a single process.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This container runs the main job, not a script to launch it.
      launcher: false

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.details: Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH. You MUST install libgomp1.

context.optimize:
You MUST maximize the LAMMPS FOM, k-atom or m-atom steps per second. 
You MUST execute in the pwd with lmp -v x 16 -v y 16 -v z 16 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite      
You MUST choose instance type and resources that will maximize the FOM.
context.resources:
The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. For your optimization you can choose from the following instance types, and you will need to add the correct nodeSelector with the node.kubernetes.io/instance-type label indicating your choice. You are still limited to one node.
  c7a.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, AMD

  c6in.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
